clue.text: U-boat then plane boarded by China's principal citizen

parts.note: a U-boat is a submarine, a sub

indicators.note: something boarded by passengers has them climbing inside it

parts.note: a jet is a plane
the principal, leading letter of China

explanation.surface: A wartime passenger hops from submarine to aircraft, where a Chinese dignitary joins the flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is a member of a state owing allegiance to it, which is what a citizen is.

clue.text: Prim, strait-laced celebrity sitting on church yard

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
CH is the abbreviation for church
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A stuffy, prudish celebrity is perched on a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, sitting on puts the first part above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy describes stiff, formal behaviour, like a collar stiffened with starch.

clue.text: Robber in group stealing equipment

indicators.note: something stealing an item takes it in and holds it

parts.note: a band is a group; it wraps round
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A thief belongs to a gang that steals gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, a member of a gang that robs travellers.

clue.text: "No good leaving Blighty" — horny southern African

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Blighty is old British slang for Britain or England
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: An émigré declares England no good as they leave for southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Horny here means having horns, not anything racier.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large spiral-horned antelope of southern and eastern Africa.

clue.text: London thieves that might get into pot?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Cockney rhyming slang, tea leaf for thief
second meaning: what goes into a teapot

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a rhyming phrase: tea leaf means thief. Pot also hints at prison, where thieves end up.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang, thieves are tea leaves; literally, tea leaves are brewed in a teapot.

clue.text: Retired double-0 spy laconically carries a tune

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the joined letters are read backwards

parts.note: the second zero of the pair, read as the letter O
taken as written
the start of the word, cut short as laconic speech is

explanation.surface: A retired secret agent with a licence to kill hums a tune in his famously clipped style.
explanation.walkthrough: In effect the answer runs backwards through '0 spy lac', with the zero standing in for an O; 'carries' hints that the letters sit inside the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a West Indian song style, so one calypso is a tune.

clue.text: Auntie rising to cuddle a Yankee taxi-driver

indicators.note: in a down answer rising reads from bottom to top, backwards
cuddling wraps arms around something

parts.note: Auntie is a nickname for the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster
taken as written
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An aunt stands up to hug an American cab driver.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie, the BBC's nickname, is British knowledge; reversed it wraps A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabby is an informal word for a cab driver, that is, a taxi-driver.

clue.text: Indolent maid, one bearing many dishes

parts.note: indolent means lazy
a girl's name standing for a maid, a young woman

explanation.surface: A slothful maidservant is the one carrying loads of dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the device saves a servant's work: the dishes turn while the server stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy Susan is a rotating tray placed on a dining table to carry many serving dishes.

clue.text: Thin coating on gold table

parts.note: plate is a thin layer of metal coating
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A thin layer of gilt on a table, perhaps an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: Table is not furniture here but tableland.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a tableland, an area of high flat ground.

clue.text: Border and bed both pruned, tidied up

indicators.note: pruning trims the tops off, so each word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener has pruned the border and flower bed, leaving them neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordered means arranged neatly, put in order, which is what tidied up describes.

clue.text: Lad from Middle East — The Greatest Crimper, it's said?

parts.note: boxer Muhammad Ali's nickname was The Greatest

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want a spelling that matches the spoken word

parts.note: a crimper is a hairdresser; in a non-rhotic British accent the word sounds like this

explanation.surface: A young man from the Middle East is hailed as the finest hairdresser around.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone relies on a British accent that drops the R sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba, hero of the Arabian Nights tale, is a young man from the Middle East.

clue.text: Teammate of Neil A and Michael C gutted red bird

parts.words: Teammate of Neil A and Michael C
parts.note: Apollo 11 crew: Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Buzz Aldrin, styled the same way as Buzz A

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: only the outside letters of red survive

explanation.surface: Something about the Apollo 11 astronauts and a red bird, a space-flavoured riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue abbreviates the astronauts' surnames to initials, so the third crewman comes out as Buzz A, giving BUZZ plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzard is a broad-winged bird of prey.

clue.text: One stocks wicked items in the style of Bing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shop selling candles, items with wicks
second meaning: a jokey adjective, like Chandler Bing of the sitcom Friends

explanation.walkthrough: Wicked here means having a wick, not evil; Bing is Chandler Bing from Friends, not Bing Crosby, and adding Y makes a jokey adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandlery is a candle-maker's shop or stock, and the playful second sense means behaving like Chandler from Friends.

clue.text: Promise second wife endless years

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: without its ends means both first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone vows to give a second wife long, endless years of devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to promise solemnly, as in swearing an oath.

clue.text: Off-peak call?

parts.note: surface reading: a phone call made at the cheaper time of day
setter's reading: a call sent out from a mountain peak, as Alpine singers do

explanation.walkthrough: Off-peak is telephone-tariff language, but here it means coming off a mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodel is the warbling Alpine cry traditionally sung across mountain valleys.

clue.text: Ancestral ground, home to duchy

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: all the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Ancestral grounds belong to a noble duchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground looks like land here but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is the city giving its name to the Duchy of Lancaster, held by the British monarch.

clue.text: Branch of The Old Bill that puts the squeeze on?

definitions.text: Branch of The Old Bill that puts the squeeze on?

parts.note: surface reading: a police department, the Old Bill being British slang for the police
setter's reading: a team of workshop clamps, tools that squeeze

explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police. Putting the squeeze on sounds like intimidation, but also describes what a bench vice does.
explanation.definitionFit: A police unit dealing with gambling, prostitution and drugs, whose name also suggests a group of gripping tools.

clue.text: A mild blue Conservative, Archer is at home here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soft pale blue colour named after a university

definitions.text: Conservative, Archer is at home here
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the area where Tory peer and novelist Jeffrey Archer lives, at Grantchester

explanation.walkthrough: Blue is also the Conservative party colour, so the surface reads as a moderate Tory; Jeffrey Archer is a Conservative politician and bestselling author.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge blue is a light shade of blue, and the city near Grantchester is Archer's home.

clue.text: Mo changes, slipping into oriental dress

indicators.note: changes tells us the preceding letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: the name together with the indicator word supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Mo changes outfits, slipping into an eastern-style dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The word changes is both part of the letters and the signal that they move.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar.

clue.text: Max number allowed in vehicle touring Spain being cautious

indicators.note: touring goes round something, enclosing it

parts.note: as much as a car can hold; it wraps round
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A driver touring Spain is careful not to overload the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: E for Spain comes from España.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful and cautious both describe taking care to avoid risk.

clue.text: Saving firm involved in money changing

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside something
changing means altering the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm involved in money-changing makes a saving.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy means thrift, the act of saving money or resources.

clue.text: Horrid area Stuyvesant cleared out in New York

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the next abbreviation

parts.note: first half of the abbreviation NY, which wraps round
A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: clearing out the contents leaves just the outside letters

parts.note: only the outer letters of the name are kept
second half of the abbreviation NY

explanation.surface: A grim neighbourhood, Stuyvesant, has been cleared in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuyvesant is a Manhattan area name; NY splits round A and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and horrid are synonyms meaning very unpleasant.

clue.text: Quiet, upper-class, yet quaintly English term for sleep

parts.note: SH is a call for quiet

indicators.note: quaintly suggests an odd, unusual arrangement of the letters

parts.note: U means upper-class in British usage
taken as written, before rearranging
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A quiet, posh, yet old-fashioned English word for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is an informal word for sleep, as in getting some shut-eye.

clue.text: Provider of liquidity between banks in Wuhan?

definitions.text: Provider of liquidity between banks in Wuhan?

parts.note: surface reading: money markets lending cash between financial institutions

parts.words: Provider of liquidity between banks in Wuhan?
parts.note: setter's reading: a river, water flowing between riverbanks, passing through the Chinese city

explanation.walkthrough: Liquidity and banks are finance words, but here they mean water and riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest river and flows through the city of Wuhan.

clue.text: Major setback — million lost importing international wine

indicators.note: a setback here is a setting back, turning the word round
importing brings something inside
something lost is gone, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A huge financial reversal: a million lost by an importer of foreign wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Major setback reads as a big disaster, but it means the word major turned round; dropping its final M leaves ROJA, which takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Spanish region of that name.

clue.text: Buffoon king undressed queen at home

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer layer, so first and last letters go

parts.note: Charles is a king's name
QU is a recognised abbreviation for queen
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A clownish king strips off in front of his queen while at home.
explanation.walkthrough: King must be expanded to a particular king, Charles, before undressing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the comic servant of the commedia dell'arte, hence a clown or buffoon.

clue.text: Full of energy, tough, went like the clappers

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside

parts.note: hard means tough; it wraps round
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Someone tough and energetic charged off at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Like the clappers is British slang for very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run very fast, like a hare, so hared means sped off.

clue.text: Winger, for example, starts to relish extra time

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example

indicators.note: the starts of the following words means their first letters

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing, for example, would love some extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: Winger sounds like a footballer, but it is a creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like bird, and as a winged creature it is a winger.

clue.text: Vagrant late for training

indicators.note: training puts things into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A drifter turns up late for a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: A floater is someone who drifts from place to place or job to job, a vagrant.

clue.text: Kestrel filmed in Devon river, black as can be

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, a county in south-west England; it wraps round
Kes is the 1969 Ken Loach film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: A kestrel is filmed by a Devon river in the pitch dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Kestrel filmed is the film Kes, named after the bird; it sits inside DART.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkest is the superlative of dark, meaning as black as anything could be.

clue.text: Dearly, desperately gobbling up European cake like this?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing the cake

indicators.note: gobbling up swallows something inside
doing something desperately means wildly, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone desperately wolfs down a European cake, built up in tiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and wordplay overlap: the gobbling suggests eating a cake, which is the layered thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A layered cake is built from stacked tiers of sponge and filling, so the cake is described this way.

clue.text: Some believe X tremendous? It's immoderate

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the run starts at the end of believe and continues into tremendous

explanation.surface: Is X tremendous? Believing that would be going too far, someone says.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and immoderate both mean going far beyond what is reasonable.
